title: 2nd Grade for ME
before:
The Maine DOE is pleased to provide an open-source instructional program for second-grade classrooms.

2nd Grade for ME is an interdisciplinary, whole-student instructional program adapted from Boston Public Schools’ Focus on Second curriculum. It supports students’ growth across literacy and language, science and engineering, social studies, the arts, and social-emotional learning. Grounded in research-based practices and aligned with Maine’s Learning Results, the program fosters both academic development and student agency—as learners and as citizens. With its intentional and integrated design, 2nd Grade for ME engages students in meaningful, developmentally appropriate learning that connects thinking with doing across a range of topics.

Lesson Plans 

 
Unit 1 - How We Learn in our School Communities

Unit 1 launches the school year by guiding children and teachers in exploring the purpose of school and deepening their understanding of learning and learners, with a focus on fostering inclusive environments and meaningful interactions.

Go to Unit 1

Unit 2 - The Forces of Wind & Water

Unit 2 highlights science through a study of how wind and water shape and reshape the land. It invites students to question the stability of the ground beneath us and to recognize that, across the world, Earth’s surface is constantly changing. In this unit, students investigate the effects of wind and water on land and explore how people adapt to and interact with these natural forces.

Go to Unit 2

Unit 3 - Connecting Places, Connecting People

In Unit 3, students will learn about important topics in hands-on and meaningful ways. With support from their teachers, students examine books, pictures, artwork, and ideas closely to gain a deeper understanding of the world around them. Children explore science and engineering, learn about Maine’s history and communities, and work with new and familiar materials. Through projects, students share their thinking and show what they have learned in creative and exciting ways.

Go to Unit 3

Unit 4 - The Power of Pollinators

Unit 4 invites second graders to explore how plants and animals depend on one another. Through the study of birds, bees, butterflies, bats, and flowering plants, students investigate the process of pollination and its role in ecosystems and food systems. Students observe plant growth by planting seeds and documenting changes over time. As they explore life cycles and plant structures, they consider how form and function support survival and reproduction. Through observation, discussion, and hands-on investigation, students build an understanding of interdependence in the natural world and the importance of pollinators in their environment.

Go to Unit 4

notes: 1 section header — too few for a contents list.
460 words with no section headers at all — the biggest single improvement available here.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 1 heading sits at a level the page never opens — "2nd Grade for ME" is an h3 with no h2 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 3 links on this page open a file — 2 Word, 1 Excel — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Put the card titles on one level
decisions.why: 4 card titles are written at a level copied from an example rather than chosen — h5 on a page whose sections are h2. Only the number changes.

decisions.label: Left-align a section header
decisions.why: 1 section header is centred, where 1,103 of the 1,139 on the site are left-aligned — the component list says not to centre them. The band runs the full width of the column, so a centred title has no fixed relationship to anything else, and a two-line one breaks the left edge every other heading shares. Only the alignment changes.

decisions.label: Remove the first section header
decisions.why: "2nd Grade for ME" repeats the page title, so the reader is told the same thing twice before any content.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: The Maine DOE is pleased to provide an open-source instructional program for second-grade classrooms.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.
